candidate_result_row_amendment.claim: In codes/loop/loop.sbatch the .failcount accounting, the minimum-runtime penalty, the breaker and the scancel of the queued afterany successor live in one function, finalize(), run from an EXIT trap installed immediately after resubmit(), and finalize sorts the ways a link can end into five classes rather than two. A deliberate storage stop -- the loop exiting 3 WITH $BASEDIR/STOP present, the file the loop writes before that exit -- cancels the successor and spends no attempt. A scheduler termination -- SIGTERM to this wrapper, recorded by a TERM trap installed before the resubmit, or a 128+15 loop status on a link that has run at least KTG_MIN_RUNTIME_SECONDS -- leaves .failcount untouched and KEEPS the queued successor, which is the resume itself. A pre-flight failure counts, with the fast-failure penalty, and cancels the successor, which would repeat it. A loop failure counts and cancels only when the breaker trips; an exit 3 without STOP is one of these. A cycle that ran and exited 0 resets the count, and an exit 0 that never ran the loop leaves it. Neither loop.sbatch nor synchronous_loop_9x9.sh contains a storage threshold or its own du/df/quotas.py measurement: both call codes/data_budget/scratch_guard.sh and honour its exit code, with no --root passed, so the only storage numbers in force are budget.env's. codes/loop/export_model_for_selfplay_9x9.sh no longer names the TensorFlow-era exporter anywhere. The three upstream defect repairs (o09, o13 config half, o17) admitted in the first row are unchanged. NOT covered: a SIGKILL end -- KillWait expiry, cgroup OOM, node failure -- runs no handler, writes nothing and simply lets the queued successor resume; that is by design and its executed proof is o25's.
